title: Sound unit quiz
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Sound (Misty Mountain, Sierra and How Can We Change a Sound?)
source: Seeded from science/y4 lesson 25 (Sound unit quiz (portal worksheet with answer key))
intro: Covers lessons 15 to 25 of Sound (Misty Mountain, Sierra and How Can We Change a Sound?). Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Which can sound NOT travel through?
questions.a: C) A vacuum. A vacuum has no particles to pass on the vibrations.

questions.q: Which is best for muffling sound?
questions.a: B) A thick woolly jumper. Soft, thick materials absorb vibrations; hard ones reflect them.

questions.q: Which makes the highest pitch?
questions.a: B) Ruler 10 cm over the edge. A shorter part vibrates faster, so the pitch is higher.

questions.q: Which band gives the lowest pitch?
questions.a: B) Thick and loose. Thick and loose both slow the vibrations, so the pitch is lowest.

questions.q: You hit a drum harder. What changes?
questions.a: A) It gets louder. Harder means bigger vibrations, so louder; the pitch stays about the same.

questions.q: Which is loudest?
questions.a: C) 80 dB. A bigger number of decibels means a louder sound.

questions.q: You move from 2 steps to 8 steps away. The sound is...
questions.a: B) Fainter. Further from the source the vibrations have spread out, so it is fainter. Pitch does not change.

questions.q: Testing water amount and pitch. What do we keep the same?
options: The glass and how hard we tap
questions.a: B) The glass and how hard we tap. The water changes; everything else stays the same.

questions.q: Test 1 and test 2 gave the same answer. This shows...
questions.a: A) The result is reliable. Matching repeats give us more confidence in the result.

questions.q: Which sentence explains WHY?
options: Slower vibrations make a lower pitch
questions.a: B) Slower vibrations make a lower pitch. A 'why' sentence uses the science of vibrations.

questions.q: You pluck a band harder. What changes?
questions.a: B) Volume. Harder plucking gives bigger vibrations: louder, same pitch.

questions.q: Sounds are made by...
questions.a: Vibrations

questions.q: Does sound get louder or fainter as you move away?
questions.a: Fainter

questions.q: Sound travels through...
questions.a: Solids, liquids and gases

questions.q: Can sound travel through a solid?
questions.a: Yes

questions.q: Sound cannot travel through a...
questions.a: Vacuum

questions.q: Soft materials...
questions.a: Absorb sound

questions.q: Which material muffles sound best?
questions.a: A soft, thick one

questions.q: What is an echo?
questions.a: Sound that bounces back

questions.q: Shorter vibrating objects make...
questions.a: Higher pitch
